facts.statement: The genus is known from a single partial vertebra that possesses unusual features not found in other sauropods.
facts.quote: It is known from a single partial vertebra with unusual features, unlike those of other sauropods.

facts.statement: Fossil collector Philip James Rufford discovered the vertebra in the early 1890s.
facts.quote: Discovery and history Fossil collector Philip James Rufford discovered the vertebra that would be later named Xenoposeidon in the early 1890s.

facts.statement: The fossil was found near Hastings in East Sussex, England, within the Hastings Bed Group.
facts.quote: It was found near Hastings in East Sussex, England, in rocks of the Hastings Bed Group.

facts.statement: The specimen was briefly described by Richard Lydekker in 1893.
facts.quote: The partial posterior back vertebra, cataloged as BMNH R2095, was briefly described by English naturalist and paleontologist Richard Lydekker in 1893.

facts.statement: The bone remained largely unnoticed for 113 years while stored at the British Natural History Museum in London.
facts.quote: The bone attracted little attention for decades, sitting on a shelf at the British Natural History Museum in London for 113 years.

facts.statement: The new genus was officially announced by the British Palaeontological Association on November 15, 2007.
facts.quote: The new genus was first announced by the British Palaeontological Association on November 15, 2007.

facts.statement: Researchers initially classified Xenoposeidon as a neosauropod of uncertain affinities because it did not fit comfortably into established groups.
facts.quote: Xenoposeidon could be a derived member of one of the known groups, or may even represent a new group. The authors left it as a neosauropod of uncertain affinities.

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Taylor reclassified Xenoposeidon as a basal member of Rebbachisauridae, placing it 10 million years older than Histriasaurus.
facts.quote: However, a study published in 2018 by Taylor recovered X. proneneukos as a basal member of Rebbachisauridae, and 10 million years older than the next oldest member of the family, Histriasaurus.

facts.statement: Xenoposeidon belongs to the parent group Rebbachisauridae.
The family of Xenoposeidon is Rebbachisauridae.
Xenoposeidon is classified within the class Saurischia.
Xenoposeidon lived during the Berriasian to Valanginian stages, between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (139.1 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Xenoposeidon was a large quadrupedal herbivore, similar to other sauropods.
facts.quote: Like other sauropods, Xenoposeidon would have been a large quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest the type individual was between 15 and 20 meters long and weighed between 2.8 and 7.6 tonnes, depending on its body proportions.
facts.quote: Extrapolating from the vertebra suggests that the type individual of Xenoposeidon could have been about 15 m long and weighed approximately 7.6 tonnes (8.4 short tons), if it resembled Brachiosaurus, to 20 m long and 2.8 tonnes (3.1 short tons), if it was built like the longer, lighter Diplodocus.

facts.statement: The centrum of the preserved vertebra is estimated to be 200 mm long, with a preserved height of 300 mm.
facts.quote: The centrum is estimated at 200 mm long, and the height of the preserved portion of the vertebra is 300 mm.

facts.statement: The posterior face of the centrum has an average diameter of 165 mm and features a concave surface.
facts.quote: The average diameter of the posterior face of the centrum is 165 mm, with a concave surface.

facts.statement: The neural arch leans forward at an angle of 35 degrees and has broad areas of featureless bone on its lateral surfaces.
facts.quote: The neural arch leans anteriorly at 35° and there are broad areas of featureless bone on the lateral surfaces of the arch.

facts.statement: The neural canal is large and teardrop-shaped at the front but small and circular at the back opening.
facts.quote: The neural canal is large and teardrop-shaped anteriorly but small and circular at its posterior opening.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses have classified Xenoposeidon as a nomen dubium because the fossil material is considered nondiagnostic.
facts.quote: The titanosauriform phylogeny by D'Emic established Xenoposeidon as a nomen dubium due to its basis on nondiagnostic material.

rejected.statement: Xenoposeidon is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England that lived approximately 140 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Xenoposeidon (meaning "strange or alien Poseidon", in allusion to Sauroposeidon) is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England, living about 140 million years ago.
